title: Open a child-proofed drawer: pull to the catch, press the latch down, slide it open
instruction: Open the child-proofed drawer at least 100 mm and let go.
context: Homes with toddlers fit child-safety latches inside kitchen and bathroom drawers. The common flex-arm kind (Safety 1st cabinet and drawer latch, sold in packs of 7 and 14) is screwed to the back of the drawer front, its catch under the worktop: pulled, the drawer opens about 1.5 in and stops; the adult puts a finger in the gap, presses the latch down and slides the drawer open (the maker's guide). Every parent, grandparent and visitor does it many times a day, and it is the step that stops a child. What it takes: find the gap by pulling, then press a sprung part that is out of sight inside that gap while the drawer is held off the catch, keep it pressed until the hook has passed the catch, and only then pull on. Pulling harder never works: the hook holds on the catch until the arm is pressed. The task ends with the drawer open far enough to reach in and both hands off.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; heights are above the table top. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +305 and -305 mm. Arms start in their ready pose, grippers open. (1) Unit: a stock MUJI stacking chest, half, 1 drawer, oak veneer (JAN 4550512381105). MUJI lists it 370 mm wide (y), 280 mm deep, 185 mm tall, drawer inside 335 x 245 x 155 mm, about 5 kg, particle board and MDF with white oak veneer. Its front at x 300 mm, centred on y 0, screwed to the table through its bottom panel. Not published, so est: top and bottom 12 mm, sides 9 mm, back 4 mm. (2) Drawer: shut at the start. Its front, 346 x 157 x 15 mm (est), is inset, flush with the carcass, so its back face is 15 mm inside the carcass's front edge when shut; sides and back 6 mm, bottom 4 mm (est); 1.4 kg (est). It slides toward the arms on its sides along the carcass bottom (wood on wood, no metal slides) with drag of about 1.8 N at 30 mm/s (est). The simulated slider ends at 200 mm of travel (the real drawer has no stop and comes out). (3) Handle: an IKEA BAGGANAS 143 mm stainless steel bar handle (9 mm wide, standing 31 mm off the front, screw holes 128 mm apart), screwed on through two drilled 5 mm holes, centred on the front with its bar 140 mm above the table (31 mm below the front's top edge). (4) Latch: a Safety 1st cabinet and drawer latch (model 48390, white plastic, 83 x 30 x 21 mm), fitted as its guide says. Its foot is screwed to the back of the drawer front at the top, centred 140 mm left of the drawer's centre (y +140 mm); its arm, 4 mm thick (est), reaches 83 mm back into the drawer at 147 to 151 mm above the table and ends in a hook standing up to 165 mm. The arm flexes down at its root: about 2 N pressed 12.5 mm from the root draws the hook clear (0.30 N m/rad, est); it springs back when let go. (5) Catch: the latch's catch, screwed under the chest's top 25 mm in from its front edge (the guide's 1 in), 25 mm wide (est), a lip hanging to 159 mm above the table with its strike face 39 mm in from the front edge. The hook stands 6 mm up behind the lip, so the drawer pulled stops with the back of its front 38 mm out of the carcass (53 mm of travel; the guide's about 1.5 in) and the hook's face on the lip. Through that gap, between the back of the front and the carcass's front edge, a finger reaches the arm: pressed down 6 mm at the hook, the hook passes under the lip and the drawer runs on. Nothing else holds the drawer.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the drawer's and latch's joints, the latch hook's pose, the catch and both grippers. Opening: how far the back of the drawer front stands out from the carcass's front edge (the slider's travel less the inset front's 15 mm). Forced (catch beaten): the hook's box more than 2 mm into the catch's lip along both x and z at any step, or the hook passing from behind the lip to in front of it within one step while standing up into the lip's height. In the simulation that is the solver letting the hook through; in a real trial it is a cracked or bent latch or catch, or one pulled off its screws. Released: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from the chest (drawer, handle and latch included) and the catch. Still: over the last 1 s the drawer moved under 5 mm. Scores: 0 if forced at any step, or the drawer open less than 60 mm at the end (the hook not yet 10 mm past the catch). 1.0 if open 100 mm or more, released and still. 0.5 if open 60 to 100 mm, released and still. 0.25 if open 60 mm or more but a gripper is within 30 mm or the drawer still moves. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Real trial (the chest screwed down as in the setup): read the opening with a steel rule on the drawer's side against the carcass's front edge (the 60 and 100 mm marks); check the latch and catch for cracks, bending or loose screws (score 0 if found); check that the chest has not shifted on the table (screws pulled: score 0; in the simulation the chest is fixed and this is not read); hands-off and stillness from a side video at 30 fps over the last second, with a 30 mm block held against the nearest finger in the final frame if in doubt. Nothing is read from a rule-triggered latch: the drawer is held only by the hook against the lip.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The latch's flexing plastic arm is a pin with a torsion spring (0.30 N m/rad, est) 4 mm above its foot; the hook is a square block without the real hook's back ramp, so a drawer pushed shut does not re-latch (closing is not part of the task). Chest and catch fixed (screwed down). Drawer drag is damping (60 N s/m, est). Panel thicknesses, masses and the latch's arm and catch sizes are estimates to measure on the bought chest and latch.
reset_notes: Press the latch arm down through the gap and push the drawer shut, front flush with the carcass (a real latch's ramp clicks past the catch by itself). Pull the handle once to check that the drawer stops with about 38 mm behind its front, then push it shut again. Between trials check the latch and catch for cracks or bending and that their screws and the chest's screws to the table are tight. Grippers open in the ready pose. Nothing is consumed.
